Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

EarthFlux 0.0.0.9000 (development version)

First development version. It sets up the package infrastructure and provides the core physics of the METRIC surface energy balance chain as numeric functions, from net radiation to daily actual evapotranspiration (milestone M2), and the meteorological forcing of that chain: weather station tables and their quality control, reference evapotranspiration at the stations and the regionalization of station variables over the working grid by geographically weighted regression and its baselines (milestone M3). Most formulations are candidates pending verification against the primary references; no scientific result has been validated yet.

New features

METRIC core chain

  • ef_net_radiation() computes the instantaneous net radiation at the land surface from incoming shortwave radiation, albedo, incoming longwave radiation, emitted longwave radiation and surface emissivity (METRIC surface radiation balance), keeping the reflected incoming longwave term explicit. Inputs are validated (type, recycling and physical domain, with classed errors) and missing values propagate. The form of the equation is corroborated by secondary sources; verification against the primary reference (Allen et al., 2007) is pending.

  • Radiation components that produce the inputs of ef_net_radiation() (all CANDIDATA except where stated; unverified choices are explicit arguments without defaults):

    • ef_solar_geometry() returns, per pixel and overpass instant (numeric doy of the UTC date and utc_hour, angles in radians), the cosines of the solar zenith angle and of the incidence angle on the tilted pixel plane (GIS aspect), the declination, the hour angle and the inverse relative Earth-Sun distance. The calendar terms and the hour angle are verified against FAO-56; the equation of time is applied exactly once.
    • ef_tau_sw() (with an explicit method) dispatches to ef_tau_sw_allen(), the clear-sky shortwave transmissivity split into direct-beam and diffuse parts (function of zenith angle, pressure, vapour pressure and an explicit turbidity), and ef_tau_sw_elevation(), the simple elevation form.
    • ef_atm_emissivity() computes the effective atmospheric emissivity from the clear-sky transmissivity.
    • ef_rs_in() (with an explicit method) dispatches to ef_rs_in_modelled() (clear-sky) and ef_rs_in_measured() (measured radiation with a given diffuse fraction); both project the direct-beam, diffuse and ground-reflected components onto the pixel plane.
    • ef_rl_in() computes the incoming longwave radiation from an effective atmospheric emissivity and a temperature whose choice (air, cold-pixel or pixel surface temperature) is left to the caller, and ef_rl_out() the longwave radiation emitted by the surface.

  • ef_air_pressure() computes the mean atmospheric pressure from elevation (FAO-56 Eq. 7), shared by the radiation, sensible heat and reference evapotranspiration modules.

  • ef_g() estimates the instantaneous soil heat flux with an explicit method and no default, returning G, the ratio G/Rn and the branch applied. The methods are also available as ef_g_bastiaanssen() (SEBAL, function of surface temperature, albedo and NDVI) and ef_g_tasumi() (METRIC, function of LAI, with a bare-soil branch for LAI < 0.5). Both formulations are candidates: verification against the primary references is pending. Impossible inputs raise classed errors; values of G are never truncated.

  • Anchor pixels of the METRIC calibration (stage [A], selection): ef_select_anchors() selects the cold and hot anchor pixels from numeric vectors or matrices of surface temperature, NDVI, albedo and, optionally, LAI and land cover, following explicit criteria built with ef_anchor_criteria(), ef_anchor_rule(), ef_homogeneity() and ef_anchor_pick(). There are no default thresholds and nothing is relaxed without an explicit plan. The result (class earthflux_anchors) records the anchor pixels and their attributes, exactly one calibration point per class with an explicit aggregate, the dispersion of the anchor values, the computed thresholds, the funnel of candidates, the search domain used, flags and provenance. ef_anchors() builds the same object from cells or coordinates chosen by the user. Missing candidates, an empty percentile domain, inverted anchors, anchors outside the grid and missing temperatures raise classed errors. No selection criterion is verified against a primary source (CANDIDATA).

  • ef_anchor_conditions() adds the boundary conditions at the anchor pixels (stage [B]): target latent heat flux from an explicit cold-anchor reference ET fraction and an explicit hot-anchor condition (etrf_hot or le_hot), with the instantaneous reference ET and the latent heat of vaporization evaluated at each anchor pixel, and the target sensible heat flux H = Rn - G - LE consumed by the sensible heat calibration. The latent heat is obtained with the same conversion as ef_et_inst(). Optional roughness length, blending-height wind speed and pressure are passed through to the calibration points, which then hold every input of the sensible heat calibration. The forms are CANDIDATA; no coefficient has a default.

  • Aerodynamics of the METRIC sensible heat flux: ef_zom() dispatches, with an explicit method and no default, to the momentum roughness length methods ef_zom_lai(), ef_zom_ndvi(), ef_zom_perrier() and ef_zom_height(); ef_blending_wind() extrapolates the station wind to the blending height; ef_ustar() and ef_rah() compute the friction velocity and the aerodynamic resistance to heat transport, with optional stability corrections. No minimum roughness, terrain factor or wind floor is applied (not verified). All forms are CANDIDATA; the heights (blending height, z1, z2) and the station roughness have no defaults.

  • ef_air_density() (FAO-56 form, temperature in K), ef_ts_datum() (surface temperature referred to an elevation datum), ef_dt_coef() (coefficients of dT = a + b Ts_datum from the hot and cold anchors) and ef_sensible_heat() (H = rho cp dT / rah).

  • ef_calibrate_h() calibrates dT from one calibration point per anchor class, iterating the aerodynamic resistance with the Monin-Obukhov stability correction at the anchors (phase A, with a closure so that the anchors reproduce their target H exactly) and, optionally, per pixel with the calibrated coefficients (phase B, invariant to splitting the scene into blocks). It returns an earthflux_h_calibration object with the coefficients, the convergence trace, the anchor state, the pixel results, diagnostic flags and provenance. Non-convergence returns the last iterate with an earthflux_convergence_warning and the critical flag EF_H_CALIBRATION_NOT_CONVERGED; invalid anchor states raise earthflux_calibration_error. ef_h_control() sets the convergence settings (tol = 0.01, maxit = 20, damping = 0) and requires the height of the stable momentum correction, stable_psi_m_height, because that choice is still open (decision SH-11); with a stable cold anchor it decides whether the calibration converges.

  • ef_lambda() returns the latent heat of vaporization in J kg-1 with an explicit method and no default: the FAO-56 constant ("constant") or the FAO-56 function of the air temperature in K ("fao56"). The same function is meant to be used throughout the METRIC chain.

  • ef_latent_heat() computes the instantaneous latent heat flux as the residual of the surface energy balance, LE = Rn - G - H (FAO-56, chapter 1, Eq. 1). Negative values are returned unchanged, never set to zero.

  • ef_et_inst() converts the latent heat flux (W m-2) into instantaneous evapotranspiration (mm h-1) with the latent heat of vaporization from ef_lambda() and the density of water, writing the factor 1000 mm m-1 explicitly. A unit guard rejects lambda outside [1e6, 1e7] J kg-1 (for example a value given in MJ kg-1).

  • ef_etrf() computes the reference evapotranspiration fraction ET_inst / ETr_inst, and ef_et_daily() extrapolates it to daily actual evapotranspiration with an explicit method and no default; the only method is "etrf" (ef_et_daily_etrf(), ETa_24 = ETrF * ETr_24). Both require the reference crop ("alfalfa" or "grass") explicitly. A non-positive instantaneous reference ET or a negative daily reference ET is a classed domain error. These formulations are corroborated by secondary sources; verification against Allen et al. (2007) is pending.

Dispatchers, flags and provenance

  • Every dispatcher of a method family (ef_tau_sw(), ef_rs_in(), ef_g(), ef_zom(), ef_et_daily()) takes method as its last argument, with no default, and returns a classed list with the values of the method ($total, $g, $zom, $eta_24, …), method, diagnostic flags and provenance (including the flag codes evaluated); the method functions (ef_tau_sw_allen(), ef_g_tasumi(), …) return plain numeric values. The classes are earthflux_sw_transmissivity (always with total, and with beam and diffuse set to NULL when the method gives no partition), earthflux_incoming_shortwave, earthflux_soil_heat_flux, earthflux_roughness_length and earthflux_daily_et. A required input that is missing at a position is flagged EF_INPUT_NA.

  • Results carry a flag record only for the conditions that hold somewhere; the codes that were evaluated are listed in provenance$flags_evaluated, so that “evaluated and absent” is distinguishable from “not evaluated”.

  • Diagnostic flags registered for the METRIC stages (values are never truncated or corrected):

    • radiation: EF_RAD_SELF_SHADED, EF_RAD_ATM_EMISSIVITY_GT1, EF_RAD_RS_GT_RA and EF_RAD_RN_NEGATIVE;
    • soil heat flux: EF_G_RN_NONPOSITIVE, EF_G_RATIO_NEGATIVE, EF_G_AVAILABLE_NONPOSITIVE and EF_G_LOW_LAI_BRANCH;
    • anchor pixels: EF_ANCHOR_USER_SUPPLIED, EF_ANCHOR_CRITERIA_RELAXED, EF_ANCHOR_SEARCH_EXPANDED, EF_ANCHOR_HOMOGENEITY_DROPPED, EF_ANCHOR_WINDOW_INCOMPLETE, EF_ANCHOR_TIES, EF_ANCHOR_SINGLE_PIXEL, EF_ANCHOR_COLD_H_NEGATIVE, EF_ANCHOR_HOT_LE_ASSUMED_ZERO and EF_ANCHOR_OVERPASS_SPREAD; flags evaluated upstream in an anchor cell are inherited, not duplicated;
    • sensible heat flux: EF_H_USTAR_INVALID, EF_H_PIXEL_NOT_CONVERGED, EF_H_DT_EXTRAPOLATED_HOT, EF_H_DT_EXTRAPOLATED_COLD, EF_H_NEGATIVE, EF_H_GT_AVAILABLE (cell) and EF_H_CALIBRATION_NOT_CONVERGED, EF_H_DT_SLOPE_NONPOSITIVE (object, critical);
    • evapotranspiration: EF_ET_NEGATIVE, evaluated on each ET layer.

Meteorological forcing

  • ef_station_table() builds the standard table of weather station data: station metadata and observations as two plain data frames joined by station_id, with timestamps stored in UTC (character timestamps need an explicit format and time zone), air temperature in degrees Celsius, the other variables in the units of the contract, coordinates in WGS84 ("EPSG:4326") and mandatory period semantics (timestamp_convention, interval) in the provenance. Unit conversions are applied only when declared and are recorded; exact duplicated records are kept once and conflicting ones are an error. Invalid metadata raise classed errors (earthflux_station_field_error, earthflux_station_time_error, earthflux_station_unknown_id, earthflux_station_duplicate, earthflux_station_provenance_error, all subclasses of earthflux_input_error, and earthflux_domain_error).

  • ef_station_qc() runs the quality control of the station table and never modifies the observations: it returns the long audit table $qc, equivalent record-scope flag records, the status of each value (ok, warning, excluded) under an explicit qc_policy (default "exclude_critical") and the counts in the provenance. Registered codes: EF_WS_OUT_OF_DOMAIN and EF_WS_TMIN_GT_TMAX (physical or logical impossibilities, severity critical), EF_WS_RH_GT100, EF_WS_TDEW_GT_TAIR (dew point above air temperature, or vapour pressure above the saturation vapour pressure), EF_WS_RS_GT_RA (mean solar radiation above the extraterrestrial radiation of the record window), EF_WS_TIME_GAP, EF_WS_TIME_IRREGULAR, EF_WS_HEIGHT_MISSING and EF_WS_HEIGHT_NONSTANDARD. Negative solar radiation and precipitation are physical impossibilities. Tests that need a threshold without a documented reference (plausible ranges, persistence, steps, …) are not evaluated and are listed as such in the provenance.

  • Derived meteorological variables, verified against the FAO-56 equations and worked examples (air temperature in degrees Celsius, angles in radians, radiation in MJ m-2 per day or per period): ef_psychrometric() (psychrometric constant), ef_es() and ef_es_slope() (saturation vapour pressure and the slope of its curve), the actual vapour pressure from the dew point (ef_ea_dewpoint()), from hourly temperature and relative humidity (ef_ea_rh()), from daily extremes with an explicit method (ef_ea_daily(): "rhmax_rhmin", "rhmax", "rhmean", and the ASCE-EWRI (2005) forms "rhmin" and "rhmean_tmean") and from the minimum temperature with an explicit aridity correction (ef_ea_tmin()), ef_dewpoint(), ef_wind_2m() (logarithmic profile over short grass), ef_ra_daily() and ef_ra_period() (extraterrestrial radiation per day and per hourly or shorter period, reusing the solar geometry of the METRIC core; an explicit standard selects the FAO-56 midpoint criterion or the ASCE-EWRI limits of integration at sunrise and sunset) and ef_rso() (clear-sky radiation from elevation). Relative humidities above 100 % are computed, never truncated.

  • Reference evapotranspiration: ef_ref_net_radiation() (net radiation of the reference surface, daily or hourly, with an explicit standard for the Stefan-Boltzmann constant and the limits of Rs/Rso; a carried-over cloudiness term can be supplied for night-time periods) and ef_ref_soil_heat_flux() (soil heat flux of the reference surface) feed ef_ref_et(), which computes the grass (ETo) or alfalfa (ETr) reference evapotranspiration with explicit reference, timestep and standard and no defaults, and returns an earthflux_reference_et object with flags and provenance. The FAO-56 grass equations reproduce FAO-56 examples 18 and 19. The constants of the ASCE-EWRI (2005) standardized equation (short and tall reference, daily and hourly day and night coefficients, soil heat flux ratios) and the rest of its reference ET chain are verified against the January 2005 Task Committee report (equation, table and page cited in the documentation); its worked examples (Appendix C) are not reproduced yet, as the appendices were not available. FAO-56 with the alfalfa reference is a classed error (earthflux_undefined_reference). Negative reference ET is kept and flagged.

  • Diagnostic flags of the reference ET stage: EF_WS_RS_RSO_LIMITED (the ratio Rs/Rso is limited to the range of the standard inside the cloudiness term, at most 1 for FAO-56 and between 0.3 and 1 for ASCE-EWRI; Rs is not modified) and EF_WS_ETR_NEGATIVE (negative reference ET, kept).

  • ef_station_ref_et() computes the reference ET series of every station of a quality-controlled station table (hourly or daily records), using only the values not excluded by the QC policy, and from it the instantaneous reference ET at given overpass times (etr_inst, mm h-1; option "O1", the period that contains the time, or "O3", linear interpolation between period mid-points) and the daily reference ET of given dates (etr_24, mm d-1; sum of the 24 hourly values of complete days, or the daily record). The open choices are explicit arguments without defaults: humidity source, day definition (UTC or local standard time with a UTC offset) and completeness rule, day/night criterion (extraterrestrial or net radiation above zero, the latter the ASCE-EWRI definition), night-time cloudiness (ratio of the period 2-3 hours before sunset, the ASCE-EWRI rule of the last period with a sun angle above 0.3 rad, or a fixed ratio) and the overpass method. It reproduces FAO-56 examples 18 and 19 and returns an earthflux_station_ref_et object whose flags name the table they refer to; days without all their periods (EF_WS_INCOMPLETE_DAY) and overpass times outside the records (EF_WS_OVERPASS_OUTSIDE_RECORDS) give NA and are flagged.

Spatial regionalization

  • ef_regionalize() regionalizes one meteorological station variable over the working grid for every target time and returns an earthflux_surface: the surface (SpatRaster, one layer per target time, in memory or in a file), an integer flag word per cell and target time with its bit table, the fitted model of every target time, the station table (observed and fitted values, residuals, leave-one-out residuals, exclusions with their reason), flags and provenance. It projects the station coordinates (WGS84) to the projected CRS of the grid, extracts the covariates at the stations from the same rasters (or takes them from a table), applies an explicit QC policy (use_qc, no default) and user exclusions, and predicts exactly at every cell by blocks of raster rows with terra; the block size never changes the result. It accepts the regionalization input table or the result of ef_station_qc().

  • One interface for the configurations compared in the validation plan, with no default for any scientific choice: ef_method_gwr() (C3: kernel, fixed or adaptive bandwidth, either given or selected by AICc or CV for every fit), ef_method_station() (C1: representative station, optionally with an explicit lapse rate for air temperature), ef_method_ols() (C2: global regression on the same covariates) and ef_method_idw() (C2: inverse distance weighting with a given power or one selected by leave-one-out CV on a grid). ef_predict_control() sets the block size, the output files and the write options.

  • Covariates derived from the surface state (LST, NDVI, …) must be declared in surface_covariates (decision GW-07 is open, so there is no default) and raise EF_GWR_SURFACE_COVARIATE.

  • ef_spatial_folds() builds deterministic spatial block folds (square tiles of a given side) and ef_regionalize_cv() returns the long table of out-of-fold predictions at the stations for any method, re-selecting the GWR bandwidth (or the IDW power) inside each fold by default; failed folds are reported, never dropped. The same folds serve C1, C2 and C3.

  • Optional parallelism with future.apply over target times, raster blocks and folds, only when the user has set a future plan; EarthFlux never sets a plan or changes terra options. Results are identical in sequential and parallel runs, and the execution plan is recorded in the provenance.

  • Numeric core of geographically weighted regression (GWR), implemented in base R and used by ef_regionalize(). It works on plain vectors and matrices (response, named covariates and projected coordinates in metres) and knows nothing about rasters, so that the orchestrator can call it block by block:

    • ef_gwr_fit() fits the local weighted least squares models at the stations for a fixed (metres) or adaptive (k nearest stations, counting the station itself) bandwidth, with an explicit kernel and no default ("gaussian", "exponential", "bisquare", "tricube", "boxcar" with support d <= b). The result (class earthflux_gwr) keeps the station table (fitted values, residuals, leave-one-out residuals, s_ii, local R2, bandwidth, neighbours, condition number, exclusions with their reason), local coefficients in original units, tr(S), tr(S’S), AICc, CV, the global OLS reference, the conventions applied, flags and provenance. Covariates are scaled internally for conditioning; coefficients and predictions do not change.
    • ef_gwr_bandwidth() selects the bandwidth by AICc or leave-one-out CV (explicit criterion, no default) with a recorded search set by ef_gwr_search() (log grid plus Brent refinement for fixed bandwidths, exhaustive search over k), and returns the whole criterion profile including the global model. Infeasible bandwidths (rank-deficient local designs, too few neighbours, undefined AICc or LOO) are kept in the profile and never selected.
    • ef_gwr_predict() predicts exactly at new locations (one local fit per location); results do not depend on how locations are split into blocks or chunks.
    • ef_gwr_diagnostics() collects fit statistics, the station table, the profile and the flags.
    • AICc uses n stations, sigma = sqrt(RSS/n) and tr(S), the form read in Gollini et al. (2015); it reproduces GWmodel’s AICc. Coefficients, RSS, AICc, CV, leave-one-out residuals and predictions agree with GWmodel 2.4-1 to 1e-10 in tests that run when it is installed. The formulations are candidates pending the primary references.
    • Errors: earthflux_gwr_insufficient_stations (fewer than p + 3 stations), earthflux_gwr_no_feasible_bandwidth (with the profile) and earthflux_gwr_singular_error (rank-deficient design at a station), all inheriting earthflux_gwr_error. Stations with missing values are excluded with their reason, never silently.

  • Diagnostic flags registered for the GWR stage, in the flag word of every surface (cell) or in the flag records (object, record): EF_GWR_EXTRAPOLATION_COVARIATE, EF_GWR_EXTRAPOLATION_LOCAL, EF_GWR_OUTSIDE_HULL, EF_GWR_FEW_NEIGHBOURS, EF_GWR_LOCAL_SINGULAR (cell, bits 1-5), EF_GWR_OUT_OF_DOMAIN (cell, bit 6, critical: a prediction outside the physical domain of the variable is kept and flagged, never truncated, and must be masked before the METRIC core), EF_GWR_BW_AT_BOUND, EF_GWR_BW_MULTIMODAL, EF_GWR_AICC_UNDEFINED, EF_GWR_GLOBAL_PREFERRED, EF_GWR_SURFACE_COVARIATE, EF_GWR_SINGLE_STATION (object) and EF_GWR_STATION_EXCLUDED (record).

Surface state (MODIS, in progress)

  • Internal MODIS preparation steps (not exported yet): conversion of the MOD11A1/MYD11A1 day view time (local solar time) to UTC day of year and hour per pixel, with the equation of time left to the solar geometry so that it is applied exactly once; blue-, white- and black-sky albedo from MCD43A3 with an explicit diffuse fraction; broadband emissivity from LAI; NDVI from surface reflectance; matching of 8- and 16-day composites to the LST date with the lag in days; and integer-factor aggregation to the working grid with an explicit minimum valid fraction. Options whose formulas are not verified in the specification raise earthflux_method_not_implemented.

Changes

  • Modular source layout for the surface, forcing, spatial (GWR), METRIC, diagnostics, validation and API modules.

  • Internal infrastructure for classed conditions and diagnostic flags: results are flagged, never silently corrected.

  • Physical constants (Kelvin offset, Stefan-Boltzmann constant, solar constant, von Karman constant, gravity, specific heat of air, density of water and the FAO-56 latent heat of vaporization) and the unit factors of the ET conversion are defined once, with their unit, source and verification status.

  • The registry of diagnostic flags is assembled from one table per stage (METRIC, station forcing, reference ET and regionalization) and records, for each code, its stage, severity (now including critical), scope, bit, error counterpart, specification and version. Flag records also carry their stage and scope, and the table they refer to (target) when an object holds several tables. The registry is built and validated once per session instead of at every flag record, which makes the regionalization with small blocks about ten times faster.

  • Classed conditions can carry optional data fields (for example the diagnostics of a failed calibration); new condition classes for calibration errors and convergence warnings.

  • EarthFlux imports the base package stats (sample quantiles, medians and standard deviations of the anchor selection).

  • An end-to-end test runs a synthetic scene through the whole METRIC core chain, from solar geometry to daily actual evapotranspiration, and a second one runs synthetic stations through the quality control, the regionalization of air temperature and vapour pressure (converted to kelvin at the METRIC boundary) and the station reference ET into the METRIC core.

  • GWmodel is suggested (not imported) as the cross-verification reference of the GWR core tests, which are skipped when it is not installed.

  • EarthFlux imports terra (raster input and output of the regionalization) and future and future.apply (optional parallel execution under the user’s plan, and its record in the provenance).

Documentation

  • README and introductory vignette describe the development status, show the package title from DESCRIPTION and include an executable ef_net_radiation() example.

  • pkgdown site at https://djwillichile.github.io/EarthFlux/, rebuilt on every change to main.

  • Continuous integration: R CMD check on Linux (release, devel, oldrel), Windows and macOS; a check that the roxygen2 documentation and README.md are up to date; repository settings synchronised from DESCRIPTION.
